about: The consecration of the chalice. Its words combine expressions from the institution narratives in Matthew 26, Mark 14, Luke 22 and 1 Corinthians 11. “Mystérium fídei” is not drawn from those accounts, while “ætérni” corresponds to Hebrews 13:20. The concluding command draws on Luke 22:19 and 1 Corinthians 11:25–26.

s02.translation: In like manner, after supper was ended,

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s03.narrative: The priest takes the chalice in both hands.

s04.translation: also taking this excellent chalice into His holy and venerable hands,

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s05.narrative: The priest bows his head again.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s07.narrative: Holding the chalice in his left hand, the priest makes the sign of the cross over it with his right.

s08.translation: He blessed it and gave it to His disciples, saying:

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s09.translation: Take and drink from it, all of you:

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s10.narrative: The priest speaks the words of consecration over the chalice attentively, without break and silently, holding it slightly raised.

s11.translation: For this is the chalice of My Blood, of the new and eternal covenant: the mystery of faith: which will be shed for you and for many for the remission of sins.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s12.narrative: The words spoken, the priest sets the chalice on the corporal and says silently:

s13.translation: As often as you shall do these things, you shall do them in memory of Me.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s14.narrative: The priest genuflects and adores, rises, shows the chalice to the people while the server rings the bell three times, sets it down, covers it and genuflects again.

w009.explanation: The epithet with “Cálicem” (w010) — an echo of Ps 22:5: calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est.

w040.explanation: This qualification does not occur in the institution narratives. “The blood of the eternal covenant” occurs in Hebrews 13:20.

w042.explanation: Within the very words over the chalice stands the phrase “the mystery of faith”: the Blood of the covenant named as what the Church believes.

w044.explanation: “Calix” (w035) and “Sánguinis” (w036) are both masculine, so the pronoun's form does not resolve its antecedent. English likewise leaves it open.

w050.explanation: A future at the table of the Supper: the Blood “will be shed” — the words look ahead to the Cross.

w056.explanation: The form can also mean “as often as you may have done”, but the future that follows leads to the future reading.

w058.explanation: Latin says literally “in memory of Me”. English preserves the same construction.
